Player 3then passes one penny to Player 4, who passes two pennies to Player 5, and so on, players alternately passing one penny or two to the next player who still has some pennies. $$\begin{array}{c}{\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\infty}\left(x-\frac{x^{3}}{2}+\frac{x^{5}}{2\cdot4}-\frac{x^{7}}{2\cdot4\cdot6}+\cdots\right)}\\ {\displaystyle\left(1+\frac{x^{2}}{2^{2}}+\frac{x^{4}}{2^{2}\cdot4^{2}}+\frac{x^{6}}{2^{2}\cdot4^{2}\cdot6^{2}}+\cdots\right)d x.}\end{array}$$

A–4 Let G be a group with identity e and $\phi$ :$G\rightarrow G$ a function such that 



$$\phi(g_{1})\phi(g_{2})\phi(g_{3})=\phi(h_{1})\phi(h_{2})\phi(h_{3})$$

whenever $g_{1}g_{2}g_{3}=e=h_{1}h_{2}h_{3}$ . Prove that there exists an element $a\in G$ such that $\psi(x)=a\phi(x)$ is a homomorphism (i.e.$\psi(x y)=\psi(x)\psi(y)$ for all $x,y\in G)$ 1.

$\scriptstyle\mathrm{A-}5$ Let $N_{n}$ denote the number of ordered n-tuples of positive integers $(a_{1},a_{2},\ldots,a_{n})$ such that $1/a_{1}+1/a_{2}+$ $\ldots+1/a_{n}=1$ . Determine whether $N_{10}$  is even or odd.

A-6 For a positive integer n and any real number c, define $x_{k}$ recursively by $x_{0}{=}0,x_{1}{=}1$ , and for $k\geq0$ 

$$x_{k+2}=\frac{c x_{k+1}-(n-k)x_{k}}{k+1}.$$

Fix n and then take c to be the largest value for which $x_{n+1}=0$ . Find $x_{k}$ in terms of n and $k,1\leq k\leq n$

(Here $\operatorname*{m i n}(a,b)$ denotes the minimum of a and .)

$$f(x)+f^{\prime\prime}(x)=-x g(x)f^{\prime}(x),$$

where $g(x)\geq0$ for all real x. Prove that $|f(x)|$ is bounded.

$$0\leq\sum_{i=0}^{\lfloor{\frac{2k}{3}}\rfloor}(-1)^{i}a_{k-i,i}\leq1.$$

B-5 Prove that for $n\geq2$ 

$$\overbrace{2^{2^{\cdots^{2}}}}^{n\;\mathrm{t e r m s}}\equiv\overbrace{2^{2^{\cdots^{2}}}}^{n\;-\;1\;\mathrm{t e r m s}}\pmod n.$$
